title: Author parameter.yml for fabric-cicd environment-specific configuration
description: Write the fabric-cicd parameter.yml that maps environment-specific values — lakehouse IDs, workspace IDs, connection GUIDs — so the same artifact definitions deploy across environments without hand-editing. Independent of the Service Principal, so it can proceed in parallel with task-043.
acceptanceCriteria: fabric/parameter.yml exists and validates against the fabric-cicd parameter schema.
Every hardcoded workspace/lakehouse GUID currently embedded in the notebook and pipeline definitions is represented as a parameterised value — the audit of which GUIDs those are is part of this task.
The HttpServer connection IDs used by the bronze copy activities are parameterised (they are environment-bound).
No credentials or secrets appear in the file.
A short comment block at the top states which values must change per environment and where they come from.
notes: CREATED 2026-07-29 by /work task-spec coherence audit. Spec § Next Steps & Priorities defines Phase 4 (CI/CD Deployment) with concrete deliverables, but the project had zero Phase 4 tasks — verified by a grep probe with a positive control. This task is part of the 4-task set that closes that coverage gap.
Spec anchor: § Next Steps & Priorities → Phase 4 deliverable 1, 'parameter.yml for environment-specific configuration (lakehouse IDs, connection strings)'.

PRIOR ART: memory records that Fabric dataflow connection bindings live outside the git definition and a workspace update from git silently unbinds every dataflow. Parameterising connection IDs does not fix that — call the re-bind step out explicitly so a CI deploy does not appear to succeed while leaving dataflows dead.

IMPLEMENTED 2026-07-30 (implement-agent): Authored fabric/parameter.yml against the fabric-cicd parameterization docs (github.com/microsoft/fabric-cicd/docs/how_to/parameterization.md), cross-checked against locally-installed fabric-cicd v1.2.0 (newer than spec's v0.3.x note). find_replace parameterises: workspace ID 99e4cc6d-... (9 occ across 8 notebook META blocks + pipeline_error_handler.py:705 WORKSPACE_ID), lakehouse ID 488fb9f8-... (12 occ in notebook META blocks), lakehouse artifactId ee9dfadb-... (pipeline linkedService 2 occ — same lakehouse, Fabric byte-reordered), HttpServer connections 97124587-... (bronze_EUSupplyShares copy) + 172b089e-... (bronze_GlobalSupplyShares copy). key_value_replace parameterises the 6 pipeline notebook/dataflow logicalIds (bronze-to-silver, silver-to-gold2, data_quality_checks, bronze_ingest_wgi, bronze_ingest_epi, pipeline_error_handler, bronze_azureSQLdb2table) via $items.<Type>.<displayName>.$id with the _ALL_ key (resolves per target env automatically). Out of scope: 00000000-... workspaceId sentinel (fabric-cicd fills it), 3 historical orchestrator run-ID GUIDs in pipeline_error_handler.py comments (l156/676/685), .platform/TMDL/dataflow-mashup internals. Dataflow re-bind caveat included as a bold section in the top comment block (names bronze_azureSQLdb2table, EPI_file2table, WGI_file2table; states post-deploy re-binding is a separate step NOT handled by parameter.yml). Single-environment: DEV = real current values, PROD = commented TODO placeholders (no fabricated values). Validation: yaml.safe_load passes; fabric_cicd._parameter._utils.validate_parameter_file returns True. CORRECTION to orchestrator head-start: the 4 GUIDs flagged as 'fake placeholders' (a1b2c3d4-5e6f-..., b2c3d4e5-..., d4e5f6a7-..., a1b2c3d4-e5f6-...) are the real notebook logicalIds per their .platform files — re-verified and parameterised.
